newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp sees 550 mln dm savings from merger.
newsitem.headline: Krupp sees 550 mln dm savings from merger.

text.p: The merger of the steel companies of German industry groups Thyssen and Krupp Hoesch will create annual savings of around 550 million marks, the head of the Krupp Hoesch supervisory board said.

In an interview with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung published on Thursday, Manfred Lennings said savings achieved would first be used to pay for the nearly 8,000 job cuts that would follow the merger.

His statement appears to be at odds with conditions that Ekkehard Schulz, the head of Thyssen's steel company, put on the deal on Wednesday. Schulz said Thyssen would only sign if Krupp bore the cost of job cuts, rather than Thyssen or the new company.

Thyssen and Krupp Hoesch late on Wednesday announced that they had signed a basic agreement to merge their steel companies from April 1. The new company will be called Thyssen Krupp Stahl and Thyssen will hold a majority stake of 60 percent while Krupp takes a 40 percent share.

Despite the agreement and the pledge by both companies that there would be no compulsory redundancies to achieve the reduction of the workforce, steel workers at Krupp Hoesch continued their week-long work stoppage on Thursday.
The brunt of the job cuts following the merger are expected to hit Krupp Hoesch steel operations, according to statements from the companies and unions.

Meanwhile, Thyssen's employees returned to work on Thursday, firing up the blast furnaces at the Duisburg steel mill after a week of protests appears to have died out with the assurance that Krupp, not Thyssen, will pay for the merger.

The deal between Thyssen and Krupp to arrange a friendly merger of their steel companies follows nearly a week of tense talks after Krupp launched a surprise hostile takeover bid for Thyssen, forcing its larger rival to the negotiating table.
Krupp permanently withdrew its bid for Thyssen on Monday after the two companies agreed in principle to negotiate a merger of the two steel companies Thyssen Stahl AG and Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG.
Following Wednesday's basic agreement, Thyssen and Krupp plan to work out the final details over the next four weeks.
